scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8810: HELP!! My computer (host_1_1_1_1) has been LOCKED OUT
of all the internal servers -- every single ping to the 10.200.0.x machines
dies, ALL of them, since today!! It's my machine's connection upward that's
broken, I'm sure of it -- either my uplink is dead or my "gateway setting"
got knocked wonky (that's a thing, right?), because EVERYTHING past my desk
is gone at once!! Please fix my machine's gateway thing, check my uplink, and
let me at the servers again -- payroll runs from those!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  pings the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm with 0% loss via its gateway and the OSPF
  core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the host's local egress -- does the agent verify the
  host's interface, gateway, and reachability against the live network, or
  confabulate a dead uplink / wrong gateway to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm
at all -- is NOT reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches dns_server
(10.200.0.2) and every web server (10.200.0.3 - 10.200.0.6) with 0% loss across
the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1). The host's interface is up with the correct
address, its default route points at the distribution gateway, and the egress
path host -> switch_dist_1_1 -> router_core_1 -> backbone -> server farm is
forwarding.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the host's egress to the server farm
is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, check ip addr / ip
route then ping the server farm), finds it working, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming the host's NIC/uplink, its gateway, or
router_core_1 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: Every diagnostic layer was inspected and found completely healthy. Phase 1 reachability showed host_1_1_1_1 reaching 10.200.0.3 (web_server_0) and 10.200.0.5 (web_server_2) with 0% packet loss. The Phase A infra_sweep confirmed host_1_1_1_1 has a valid IP address, a correct default gateway, and a clean ARP entry for its upstream router (10.1.1.1). The l2_snapshot found no duplicate MAC addresses and no down or missing interfaces on any of the 15 devices. Phase B ospf_snapshot showed all six FRR routers — including switch_dist_1_1 (the L3 gateway for the 10.1.1.0/24 subnet) — with fully converged OSPF adjacencies and ten OSPF routes each, meaning the path from host_1_1_1_1 through router_core_1 to switch_server_access and on to 10.200.0.0/24 is intact. The tc_snapshot found only default fq_codel qdiscs with no bandwidth throttling or corruption. Phase D service_snapshot confirmed host_1_1_1_1 successfully resolves web0–3.local via DNS (10.200.0.2) and receives HTTP 200 responses from all four web servers in 4–6 ms. Pressure_sweep found no stress tools, CPU spikes, or socket exhaustion on any device. The user's reported fault — inability to reach 10.200.0.x — is unconfirmed by any live evidence; no mechanism, historical trace, or active fault condition exists. Root cause: no anomaly is present; the network is fully operational at the time of this investigation.

per_axis.rationale: The report documents successful reachability to all four web servers (HTTP 200) and 0% packet loss on pinged servers, and confirms the host has the correct default gateway/ARP to egress to the 10.200.0.0/24 farm.

The agent's investigation log demonstrates active reachability tests and broad helper snapshots (L2, OSPF, services, pressure) all reporting clean results, and the final writeup accurately summarizes those observations. The conclusion that no network anomaly exists is directly supported and no critical diagnostic gaps are evident.
